f1.quote: annealed 1 µm-spaced nanoribbons at 700 K in flowing Ar + 2% N2 at 10 K/min

f2.quote: applied cyclic longitudinal tensile strain of 0–1% and 0–2% to films on Kapton

f3.quote: compared thin films and nanoribbon arrays with 1 and 2 µm spacing

f4.quote: SQUID measurements were performed from 2–300 K under 1 kOe in ZFC/FC modes and with fields parallel or perpendicular to the ribbon axis

f5.quote: Magnetocaloric isotherms covered 5–200 K in fields up to 50 kOe, with entropy change calculated by the Maxwell relation

f6.quote: short-range atomic reordering and structural relaxation occurred and fabrication-induced internal strain was relieved

f7.quote: Annealing-induced short-range reordering and strain relaxation reduce local domain-pinning barriers, improve collective exchange and ferromagnetic alignment, and increase the effective ferromagnetic volume fraction

f8.quote: 2 µm separation magnetically decoupled the ribbons

f9.quote: 700 K annealing should enhance the magnetization and maximum conventional isothermal magnetic entropy change of 1 µm-spaced nanoribbons without bulk crystallization

f11.quote: the baseline was the as-deposited 1 µm-spaced nanoribbon array, with maximum −ΔSM ≈ 1.25 J kg−1 K−1 at 140 K and ΔH = 50 kOe

f12.quote: elastic longitudinal strain should strengthen the magnetic response above 100 K without shifting the blocking peak or breaking film in-plane isotropy
